-health-check.name: -health-check
-health-check.description: Internal health check tool. Verifies GitHub OAuth credentials and connectivity.

list-repos.name: list-repos
list-repos.description: List repositories accessible to the current user via the Teros GitHub App (across every installation reachable). Pass `owner` to filter to a specific user/org.

params.owner: Optional filter — only return repos under this user or organization.

get-repo.name: get-repo
get-repo.description: Get detailed information about a specific repository

params.name: Repository name
params.org: Organization name. If provided, creates repo under the org.

list-issues.name: list-issues
list-issues.description: List issues for a repository with optional filters

get-issue.name: get-issue
get-issue.description: Get details of a specific issue

create-issue.name: create-issue
create-issue.description: Create a new issue in a repository

params.title: Issue title
params.assignees: Array of GitHub usernames to assign

update-issue.name: update-issue
update-issue.description: Update an existing issue. Setting `state: "closed"` closes it (use `state_reason` for completed/not_planned). `labels` REPLACES the entire label set — use add-labels-to-issue to append.

add-issue-comment.name: add-issue-comment
add-issue-comment.description: Add a comment to an issue

add-labels-to-issue.name: add-labels-to-issue
add-labels-to-issue.description: Add labels to an issue or pull request (PRs are issues in the API). Returns the full label set after the addition.

params.labels: Label names to add (case sensitive). Existing labels are preserved.

search-issues.name: search-issues
search-issues.description: Search issues and pull requests across GitHub. Use GitHub search syntax in `q` (e.g. `repo:owner/name is:issue is:open label:bug`). Returns {total_count, incomplete_results, items[]}.

params.q: Search query (GitHub search syntax). Supports qualifiers like `repo:`, `is:`, `label:`, `author:`, `assignee:`.

list-pulls.name: list-pulls
list-pulls.description: List pull requests for a repository

get-pull.name: get-pull
get-pull.description: Get details of a specific pull request

params.title: Pull request title
params.head: Branch name containing changes
params.base: Branch name to merge into (default: main)

list-pr-files.name: list-pr-files
list-pr-files.description: List files changed in a pull request. Each file includes {filename, status, additions, deletions, changes, patch?, sha, blob_url}.

list-pr-commits.name: list-pr-commits
list-pr-commits.description: List commits on a pull request. Each commit includes {sha, commit.message, author, html_url}.

list-pr-review-comments.name: list-pr-review-comments
list-pr-review-comments.description: List review comments (inline comments on diff) of a pull request. Returns array with {id, user, body, path, line, commit_id, created_at}.

request-reviewers.name: request-reviewers
request-reviewers.description: Request reviewers on a pull request. Returns the PR with `requested_reviewers` and `requested_teams` populated.

params.reviewers: GitHub usernames to request review from
params.team_reviewers: Team slugs (within the org) to request review from

create-pr-review.name: create-pr-review
create-pr-review.description: Create a pull request review. `event` controls the verdict: APPROVE / REQUEST_CHANGES / COMMENT. Returns review {id, state, user, submitted_at}.

params.body: Review body (markdown). Required for REQUEST_CHANGES and COMMENT, optional for APPROVE.
params.commit_id: SHA of the commit the review applies to (default: latest of the PR)
params.comments: Inline comments. Each item: {path, position OR line, body}.

get-branch.name: get-branch
get-branch.description: Get information about a specific branch

create-branch.name: create-branch
create-branch.description: Create a new branch from a reference

params.sha: SHA or branch name to list commits from

get-commit.name: get-commit
get-commit.description: Get details of a specific commit

compare-commits.name: compare-commits
compare-commits.description: Compare two commits or branches. `basehead` format `BASE...HEAD` (e.g. `main...feat/x`). Returns {status, ahead_by, behind_by, total_commits, commits[], files[].patch}.

params.basehead: Comparison range, format `BASE...HEAD`. May include cross-fork via `owner:ref`.

list-workflow-runs.name: list-workflow-runs
list-workflow-runs.description: List workflow runs for a repository

get-workflow-run.name: get-workflow-run
get-workflow-run.description: Get a workflow run. Returns {id, name, status, conclusion, run_number, head_branch, head_sha, html_url, created_at, updated_at, run_started_at}.

list-workflow-run-jobs.name: list-workflow-run-jobs
list-workflow-run-jobs.description: List jobs of a workflow run. Each job includes {id, name, status, conclusion, started_at, completed_at, html_url, steps[]}.

rerun-workflow-run.name: rerun-workflow-run
rerun-workflow-run.description: Re-run a workflow run. By default re-runs only failed jobs (faster + cheaper). Set `mode: "all"` to re-run every job.

params.enable_debug_logging: Whether to enable debug logging for the re-run (default: false)

cancel-workflow-run.name: cancel-workflow-run
cancel-workflow-run.description: Cancel a workflow run that is in progress. Returns {success: true} on 202 Accepted.

list-releases.name: list-releases
list-releases.description: List releases of a repository, newest first. Each release includes {id, tag_name, name, draft, prerelease, body, html_url, published_at, author}.

create-release.name: create-release
create-release.description: Create a GitHub release tagged at `tag_name`. If `target_commitish` omitted GitHub uses the default branch. Returns {id, tag_name, name, html_url, draft, prerelease, published_at}.

params.tag_name: Tag this release points to (created if missing)
params.target_commitish: Branch or SHA the tag is created from (default: repository default branch)
params.name: Release title (default: tag_name)
params.generate_release_notes: Auto-generate release notes from commits (default: false)

get-file-content.name: get-file-content
get-file-content.description: Get the content of a file in a repository

params.ref: Branch, tag, or commit SHA (default: default branch)

create-or-update-file.name: create-or-update-file
create-or-update-file.description: Create or update a file in a repo. Pass `sha` of the existing file when updating. Path must not contain `..` or start with `/`.

params.path: File path in repository (no `..`, no leading `/`)
params.sha: SHA of file being replaced (required for updates)

search-code.name: search-code
search-code.description: Search for code across GitHub repositories

get-installation-context.name: get-installation-context
get-installation-context.description: List the Teros GitHub App installations reachable by the current user, with accessible repos, granted permissions, and manage/install URLs.

get-user.name: get-user
get-user.description: List the Teros GitHub App installations reachable by the current user, with accessible repos, granted permissions, and manage/install URLs.

create-check-run.name: create-check-run
create-check-run.description: Create a check run on a commit (exclusive to GitHub Apps). The check appears in the PR/commit sidebar. Use status:in_progress while the check runs, then update with conclusion when done.

params.name: Display name of the check (e.g. "Teros review")
params.head_sha: Commit SHA the check applies to
params.output: Rich output with title, summary (markdown), optional text body
params.details_url: Optional URL with more detail (shown as link in the check)
params.external_id: Reference ID controlled by the App (idempotency on App side)

update-check-run.name: update-check-run
update-check-run.description: Update an existing check run — typically to set status:completed + conclusion when work finishes. Pass only the fields you want to change.

get-rate-limit.name: get-rate-limit
get-rate-limit.description: Read the current GitHub API rate-limit budget for the installation token. Returns per-bucket {limit, remaining, reset, used} — core, search, graphql, code_search.

dispatch-event.name: dispatch-event
dispatch-event.description: Send a `repository_dispatch` event to trigger workflows configured to listen for it. Pass `event_type` (string the workflow filters on) and optional `client_payload`.

params.event_type: Custom event type the workflow filters on (e.g. `deploy-staging`)
params.client_payload: Optional payload (max 10 properties, JSON-serializable). Available to the workflow as `github.event.client_payload`.

clone-repo.name: clone-repo
clone-repo.description: Clone a GitHub repository to the local filesystem (uses the current user access token from the Teros GitHub App). Returns {path, branch, sha, recentCommits[]}.

params.destination: Local path where the repo will be cloned (default: /workspace/<repo>)
params.branch: Branch to checkout after cloning (default: default branch)

git-status.name: git-status
git-status.description: Local git status: branch, ahead/behind vs upstream, and lists of staged, modified, untracked, and conflicted files.

params.repoPath: Absolute path to the cloned repo. If omitted, resolved as `<workspace>/<repo>`.
params.owner: Repository owner (used to resolve default repoPath).
params.repo: Repository name (used to resolve default repoPath).

git-add.name: git-add
git-add.description: Stage local changes. Pass an array of paths to stage selectively, or omit `paths` (default `.`) to stage everything.

params.paths: Paths relative to repo root. Defaults to ["."] (stage all changes).
params.update: If true, only stage already-tracked files (`git add -u`).

git-commit.name: git-commit
git-commit.description: Create a commit with the staged changes. Returns `{ sha, branch, message }`. Use `amend: true` to amend the previous commit instead.

params.message: Commit message (subject + optional body separated by blank line).
params.amend: Amend the previous commit instead of creating a new one.
params.allowEmpty: Allow creating a commit with no staged changes.
params.author: Override commit author (defaults to git config user.name/user.email).

git-push.name: git-push
git-push.description: Push commits to the remote. `force: true` uses `--force-with-lease`; `forceUnsafe: true` uses raw `--force` (destructive).

params.branch: Local branch to push. Defaults to current branch.

git-checkout.name: git-checkout
git-checkout.description: Switch branches, create a new branch, or restore specific paths. Returns the new HEAD ref. Set `force: true` to discard local changes (destructive).

params.target: Branch, tag, commit SHA, or — with `paths` — restore source.
params.paths: Restore these specific paths from `target` (no branch switch).

git-rm.name: git-rm
git-rm.description: Remove tracked files from the working tree and stage the deletion. Pass `cached: true` to only unstage (without deleting from disk).

params.paths: Paths to remove (relative to repo root).
params.cached: Only stage the deletion; keep the file on disk (`git rm --cached`).

git-mv.name: git-mv
git-mv.description: Move or rename a tracked file/directory while preserving git history. Both `from` and `to` are relative to repo root.

git-read-file.name: git-read-file
git-read-file.description: Read a file from the working tree or from a specific git revision. Pass `ref` (commit/branch/tag) to read the version at that point.

params.path: File path relative to repo root.
params.ref: Optional commit/branch/tag. If omitted, reads from the current working tree.
params.encoding: Output encoding. Use `base64` for binary files.

git-write-file.name: git-write-file
git-write-file.description: Write file content into the working tree (creates parent dirs) and stage it. Use `stage: false` to skip staging.

params.path: File path relative to repo root.
params.content: File content (utf8 by default, or base64 — see `encoding`).

git-list-files.name: git-list-files
git-list-files.description: List files in the repo, respecting `.gitignore`. Returns `{ tracked, untracked, ignored }` arrays. Optionally filter by `pattern` (glob, relative to repo root).

git-pull.name: git-pull
git-pull.description: Pull commits from the remote into the current branch. `rebase: true` for a linear history (no merge commit).

params.branch: Remote branch to pull. Defaults to upstream.
params.ff: `only` = abort if not fast-forward; `no` = always merge commit; `auto` = git default.

git-diff.name: git-diff
git-diff.description: Show differences as unified diff + numstat. Defaults to working tree vs HEAD. `from: staged` for index vs HEAD; pass `from`+`to` commit SHAs for arbitrary diffs.

params.to: Target ref when `from` is a commit. Default `HEAD` when `from`=working/staged.
params.path: Limit diff to a specific path.
params.contextLines: Number of context lines around each change.

git-log.name: git-log
git-log.description: Local commit history with structured entries. Defaults to last 20 commits on the current branch. Filter by `ref`, `path`, `author`, `since`/`until`.

params.ref: Branch / tag / commit to start from (defaults to HEAD).
params.path: Limit history to a specific path.
params.author: Filter by author (substring match).
params.since: ISO date or git-style relative (e.g. "2 weeks ago").

git-batch-commit.name: git-batch-commit
git-batch-commit.description: Apply multiple file changes (create/update/delete/rename) and create ONE atomic commit. Use this for refactors and any multi-file change where the intermediate states should not be visible in git history.

git-stash.name: git-stash
git-stash.description: Manage the stash. Default action `push` saves uncommitted changes. Other actions: pop, apply, drop, list, clear.

git-merge.name: git-merge
git-merge.description: Merge a branch/tag/commit into the current branch. On conflict, throws `GIT_CONFLICT` and the agent should resolve via `git-status` + edit + `git-add`.

params.message: Merge commit message (used when not fast-forward).
params.squash: Squash all changes into a single staged change (does NOT commit).

git-rebase.name: git-rebase
git-rebase.description: Rebase the current branch onto another ref (linear history). Or drive an in-progress rebase with `mode: continue/skip/abort`.

params.onto: Target ref to rebase onto (required unless `mode` is given).

git-reset.name: git-reset
git-reset.description: Reset HEAD to `target`. `mode: soft` keeps staging; `mode: mixed` (default) keeps working tree; `mode: hard` discards everything (destructive).

git-cherry-pick.name: git-cherry-pick
git-cherry-pick.description: Cherry-pick commits onto the current branch. Pass `commits: ["sha", ...]` or drive an in-progress pick with `mode: continue/skip/abort`.

params.noCommit: Stage changes but do not create the commit.
params.mainline: For merge commits: parent number (1-indexed) to use as mainline.

git-config.name: git-config
git-config.description: Read or write git config (whitelisted keys only). Default scope is `local` (the repo). For identity, prefer `user.name` and `user.email`.

git-tag.name: git-tag
git-tag.description: List, create, or delete local git tags. Pass `message` on create for an annotated tag (otherwise lightweight).

params.name: Tag name (required for create/delete).
params.message: If set, create an annotated tag with this message.

git-remote.name: git-remote
git-remote.description: List, add, remove, or update git remotes. `list` returns name + fetch/push URLs.

git-blame.name: git-blame
git-blame.description: Per-line attribution for a file. Returns `[{ sha, author, date, lineNumber, content }]`. Restrict with `range: "10,50"` or `ref`.

params.path: File path relative to repo root.
params.ref: Blame at a specific ref (default HEAD).

git-bisect.name: git-bisect
git-bisect.description: Binary search for the commit that introduced a bug. Workflow: start → mark each step good/bad → done. Use `reset` to abort.

params.ref: Commit to mark for `good/bad/skip` (default current HEAD).

git-fetch.name: git-fetch
git-fetch.description: Fetch refs from the remote without merging. Use `refspec` to fetch arbitrary refs (e.g. `pull/<n>/head:pr-<n>` for a PR head, `refs/tags/v1.0.0:refs/tags/v1.0.0` for a tag).

params.refspec: Optional refspec — e.g. `pull/<n>/head:pr-<n>` to bring a PR head as a local branch, or `refs/tags/<tag>` to fetch a single tag. If omitted, fetches all branches and tags from the remote.
params.depth: Limit history to N commits (shallow fetch).
params.tags: Also fetch tags (default true for default fetch, false when a refspec is provided).
params.prune: Remove local refs whose remote counterpart is gone (`--prune`).

name: GitHub
description: GitHub repository management + local git development environment - repos, issues, pull requests, actions, commits, branches, releases, plus local git operations on cloned repos (status/add/commit/push/checkout). Auth via the Teros GitHub App with user-to-server OAuth (each user actúa con su propia identidad de GitHub).

changelog.notes: Manage repos, issues, pull requests and reviews, run Actions and releases, plus full local git on cloned repos
